# 1 Clement Chapter 33 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 33 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_033_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 33

**33:1** What then shall we do, brothers? Shall we idly cease from good works and abandon love? May the Master never permit this to happen, at any rate not to us; but let us hasten with earnestness and zeal to accomplish every good work.

**33:2** For even the Creator and Master of all things himself rejoices in his works.

**33:3** For by his all-powerful might he established the heavens, and by his incomprehensible understanding he set them in order; and he separated the earth from the water surrounding it and fixed it upon the secure foundation of his own will; and by his command he ordained the living creatures that walk upon it; and having made beforehand the sea and the living creatures in it, he enclosed them by his power.

**33:4** Above all, as the most excellent and by far the greatest work of his intelligence, with his holy and faultless hands he formed man as a representation of his own image.

**33:5** For God spoke thus: "Let us make man according to our image and according to our likeness. And God made man; male and female he made them."

**33:6** Having thus finished all these things, he praised them and blessed them and said: "Increase and multiply."

**33:7** Let us observe that all the righteous were adorned in good works; even so the Lord himself, adorning himself with works, rejoiced.

**33:8** Having therefore such a pattern, let us without delay draw near to his will, and with all our strength let us work the works of righteousness.

---

*EMET renders with maximal literalness. The creation narrative (vv. 3-6) draws on Genesis 1, reinforcing Clement's argument: since God himself rejoices in good works, so should we. The divine image in man (v. 4) grounds human dignity.*
